A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaskRIS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation results, robustness evaluations, component ablations and training analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds RefClef results, referring expression comprehension experiments and further masking and distillation analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed random image masking, BERT-style text masking and shared-weight clean/masked prediction distillation remain unchanged. The corrected loss-weight equation preserves the default lambda of 0.5. Alternative masking and distillation schemes are evaluated as ablations; no changed core procedure is documented for the REC applications.

E1.justification: v2 adds segmentation evaluation on RefClef, extending beyond the three COCO-derived datasets, and adds Referring Expression Comprehension on RefCOCO (Table 3). These expand both represented data and task requirements beyond v1's segmentation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CM-MaskSD and MagNet. Table 2 adds DETRIS and a ReMamber-with/without-MaskRIS comparison; ReMamber previously appeared only in other comparisons. New REC comparisons evaluate EEVG, SimVG and C3VG, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: The established RIS splits, metrics, image resolution and training recipe remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce REC evaluation using DetAcc and additional encoder configurations, plus comparisons varying masking regions, linguistic masking schemes and auxiliary distillation. These extend the protocol without replacing the existing RIS evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds object-centric versus context versus holistic image masking (Table 5), whole-word/span/POS-based text masking (Appendix Table C), and cross-distillation (Appendix Table D). Figure 8 adds three qualitative ablation examples. Earlier component, masking-ratio, patch-size and training-loss analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Both present point estimates and training curves without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds RefClef results (75.21 oIoU for CARIS and 76.06 with MaskRIS), REC results, additional architecture comparisons and new ablation outcomes. Table 1 revises combined-training CARIS scores, including RefCOCO testA from 79.40 to 79.85 and RefCOCOg test from 69.75 to 68.73; corresponding MaskRIS scores remain unchanged. The earlier measured training times are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix Equation 5 changes from lambda times Ldist plus (1-lambda) times Lce to (1-lambda) times Ldist plus lambda times Lce. This resolves v1's contradiction with its statement that lambda=1 recovers CARIS. Other mathematical definitions and equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly extends the contribution beyond RIS to REC and positions holistic masking with pixel-level DCL against architecture-dependent, CLS-based alternatives. This broadens the claimed applicability and sharpens the novelty claim, while the abstract's original RIS performance claims and the conclusion remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations about preserving semantic anchors during text masking and the unfavorable accuracy/computation tradeoff of cross-distillation. It also interprets RefClef and REC results as supporting broader applicability. The existing limitations concerning ambiguous descriptions and difficult visual scenes are retained.

D1.justification: v2 describes the additional linguistic masking variants and acknowledges use of the NSML platform. However, it removes v1's two-A6000 hardware disclosure and measured 18.4-hour CARIS versus 16.7-hour MaskRIS training comparison. Appendix C's core implementation settings and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against masking-based RIS research, especially CM-MaskSD and MagNet, through the introduction, related work, new Figure 2 and Section 4.4. It also adds literature supporting REC comparisons, RefClef and alternative text masking strategies.

P1.justification: The contribution list, compatibility discussion and computational-cost discussion are revised, and a dedicated comparison section is added. The masking-ratio discussion moves into a reorganized appendix; affiliations, acknowledgments and citation style also change. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column journal layout with extensively repositioned displays. v2 adds a comparison diagram and several tables, expands Tables 1–2 and the qualitative masking figure, rearranges the augmentation plots side by side, and moves the masking-ratio table into the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper by addressing v1's missing comparisons with closely related masking methods and adding targeted evidence about masking choices, distillation and applicability beyond the original RIS benchmarks. Correcting Equation 5 also removes a concrete mathematical inconsistency. These gains outweigh the loss of measured runtime and hardware information, although the added experiments remain sparsely specified and some Table 1 commentary is stale after the comparator and score updates.
